document.title: Signal secure messaging for a regulated financial firm
document.produced_by: Reference sample written in the Requirements Analyzer format (see ../README.md)

application.name: Signal Server and companion services
application.summary: The open-source server behind the Signal messenger: end-to-end encrypted 1:1 and group messaging, attachments, linked devices, and voice/video calling. The chat server is a Java (Dropwizard) service; several capabilities live in companion repositories.

components.name: Chat service
components.role: WebSocket/gRPC API, message routing, accounts, keys, push

components.name: Storage service
components.role: Encrypted contacts/settings sync and groups; uses Google Cloud Bigtable

components.name: Key transparency server
components.role: Append-only log of identity keys; uses DynamoDB and DynamoDB Streams

components.name: Calling service
components.role: Selective forwarding unit for group calls

components.name: Contact discovery
components.role: Private address-book lookup inside an attested enclave

detected_signals.signal: WebSocket and gRPC listeners on the chat service
detected_signals.implies: Long-lived client connections; load balancer must support WebSocket and HTTP/2

detected_signals.signal: 34 DynamoDB tables (accounts, keys, profiles, messages, verification sessions, and more)
detected_signals.implies: DynamoDB is the primary system of record for accounts and keys

detected_signals.signal: Five separate Redis endpoints: cache, pub/sub, push scheduler, rate limiters, message cache
detected_signals.evidence: service/config/sample.yml: cacheCluster, pubsub, pushSchedulerCluster, rateLimitersCluster, messageCache
detected_signals.implies: Managed Redis with cluster mode for four endpoints; pub/sub uses a single non-cluster endpoint

detected_signals.signal: FoundationDB message store sharded across four clusters with resharding epochs
detected_signals.evidence: service/config/sample.yml: foundationDbMessages; README: 'This project uses FoundationDB'
detected_signals.implies: Self-managed FoundationDB; no managed equivalent on AWS

detected_signals.signal: Messages are cached in Redis and persisted after one minute
detected_signals.implies: Message cache must be Multi-AZ to avoid loss of undelivered messages

detected_signals.signal: Object storage for attachments and prekeys, with resumable uploads
detected_signals.evidence: service/config/sample.yml: cdn.bucket, pagedSingleUseKEMPreKeyStore.bucket, tus.uploadUri, gcpAttachments, cdn3StorageManager (gcs, r2)
detected_signals.implies: S3 buckets plus a CDN for downloads and a tus upload endpoint; upstream also uses GCS and Cloudflare R2

detected_signals.signal: Push notifications through Apple and Google
detected_signals.implies: Outbound internet egress to APNs and FCM only

detected_signals.signal: Contact discovery and secure value recovery run as remote enclave services
detected_signals.implies: Hardware-enclave hosting; the upstream enclave code targets Intel SGX

detected_signals.signal: Storage service persists to Google Cloud Bigtable
detected_signals.implies: Porting to an AWS data store, or a cross-cloud dependency

detected_signals.signal: Consumer monetisation integrations: Stripe, Braintree, Google Play and App Store billing, MobileCoin payments, donations
detected_signals.evidence: service/config/sample.yml: stripe, braintree, googlePlayBilling, appleAppStore, paymentsService, oneTimeDonations
detected_signals.implies: Not needed for an enterprise deployment; removing them shrinks third-party and payment-card scope

detected_signals.signal: Calling relies on TURN relays (Cloudflare in the sample) and a group-call SFU
detected_signals.implies: UDP media paths and public IPs for relays

detected_signals.signal: OpenTelemetry export for logs and traces
detected_signals.implies: OTel collector feeding the firm's monitoring stack

detected_signals.signal: Dynamic configuration and ASN table read from S3 every 10 seconds
detected_signals.implies: Configuration bucket with versioning and change control

detected_signals.signal: Secrets referenced indirectly as secret:// values
detected_signals.implies: Secrets manager integration; no secrets in config files

detected_signals.signal: Messages expire after 30 days in the messages table
detected_signals.implies: Server-side storage is transient and cannot serve as a record-keeping archive
Export-control review before deploying in each country

scenario.summary: A regulated broker-dealer wants a sanctioned secure messenger for employees to replace off-channel use of consumer apps. It will self-host the open-source Signal stack on AWS, keep end-to-end encryption, and still capture every business communication for record-keeping and supervision.
assumptions: 25,000 employees with up to three linked devices each (about 60,000 devices)
Peak 20,000 concurrent WebSocket connections and 2 million messages per day
Closed user group: only employees can register; no federation with the public Signal network
All devices are enrolled in the firm's mobile device management
out_of_scope: Consumer payments, donations and subscription billing
Interoperability with the public Signal service
Voice recording for roles subject to call-taping rules (calling is disabled for those roles)

functional_requirements.statement: End-to-end encrypted 1:1 and group messaging across phones, tablets and desktops, including linked devices
1:1 and group voice and video calls with relay support for restrictive networks
Attachments up to 100 MB with resumable uploads
Only active employees can register, using their corporate identity; leavers lose access within 15 minutes
Capture every message, edit, deletion, attachment and call record of in-scope employees into the firm's archive
Compliance reviewers can search, review and export captured communications, and place legal holds
Employees find colleagues through the firm directory
Users can verify each other's identity keys (safety numbers backed by key transparency)

non_functional_requirements.statement: Message content stays end-to-end encrypted; servers never handle plaintext
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero plaintext message content in the production account

non_functional_requirements.statement: All data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys; archive keys are controlled only by the compliance function
non_functional_requirements.target: 100% of stores use KMS customer-managed keys; archive key in a separate account

non_functional_requirements.statement: Only MDM-managed, attested devices can register and connect
Administrative access through SSO with MFA and no standing shell access
non_functional_requirements.target: No SSH keys; Session Manager only; break-glass access audited

non_functional_requirements.statement: Retain business communications, the first two years in an easily accessible place
non_functional_requirements.target: At least 3 years (regulatory minimum); firm policy 7 years

non_functional_requirements.statement: Records are preserved in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable form
non_functional_requirements.target: WORM storage in compliance mode; deletions impossible before retention ends

non_functional_requirements.statement: Captured communications are available to supervisory review and surveillance
non_functional_requirements.target: Delivered to the surveillance platform within 15 minutes of capture

non_functional_requirements.statement: Disappearing messages and deletions must not defeat capture
non_functional_requirements.target: Capture happens before any client-side expiry

non_functional_requirements.statement: Encryption export-control review for every country of operation
non_functional_requirements.target: Legal sign-off per country before rollout

non_functional_requirements.statement: Messaging remains available through the loss of one availability zone
Recover messaging in a second region after a regional outage
non_functional_requirements.target: RPO 5 minutes for accounts and keys; RTO 1 hour

non_functional_requirements.statement: Fast delivery to online recipients within the region
non_functional_requirements.target: p99 under 1 second from server acknowledgement to recipient device
20,000 concurrent connections and 2 million messages per day, with 3x headroom

non_functional_requirements.statement: Central logs, metrics and traces with no message content, keys or phone numbers in telemetry
non_functional_requirements.target: Automated log scrubbing checks in CI

non_functional_requirements.statement: Outbound traffic only to approved destinations
non_functional_requirements.target: Egress allowlist: APNs, FCM, corporate IdP

non_functional_requirements.statement: Message content stays in the firm's AWS accounts, except for exports to the approved surveillance platform
non_functional_requirements.target: Exports only over private connectivity; no other third party receives message content

non_functional_requirements.statement: Cost is visible per component and per environment
non_functional_requirements.target: 100% of resources tagged; monthly cost report per tier

policy_conflicts.summary: End-to-end encryption means the servers cannot read messages, yet every business communication must be captured and retained.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Capture at the endpoint: a firm-managed client build journals each sent and received message, encrypted to the archive's public key, into an isolated compliance account. Plaintext exists only on devices and inside the archive's controlled decryption step.

policy_conflicts.summary: Signal supports disappearing messages and server-side expiry, which conflicts with retention.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Disable disappearing messages through managed-client policy; journal messages at send and receive time.

policy_conflicts.summary: Upstream contact discovery and secure value recovery depend on Intel SGX enclaves, which AWS does not offer.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Replace contact discovery with the firm directory (the user group is closed and the directory is known) and disable PIN-based recovery; managed devices are re-provisioned instead.

policy_conflicts.summary: The storage service persists to Google Cloud Bigtable, which would put group and sync data with a second cloud provider.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Port the storage layer to DynamoDB.

open_questions.question: Which surveillance and e-discovery platform receives the export, and in which format?
Which roles are subject to call-recording rules and must have calling disabled?
Is the firm prepared to maintain modified forks of the AGPL-licensed server components and offer their source to users?

scoring.rubric: Mean of 12 parts: ten NFR categories (1 = numeric target, 0.5 = requirement without one, 0 = none), functional coverage, and conflict resolution; minus 0.05 per blocking open question. See ../README.md.
